'''Ernst Helmut Brandt''' (17 September 1941 – 1 September 2011) was a German [[theoretical physicist]]. He is best known for working on the [[Abrikosov vortex]] lattice in [[type-II superconductors]], particularly with the ideal lattice, its nonlocal elastic response, lattice defects, [[flux pinning|pinning]] and geometrical effects in the electromagnetic response of [[superconductors]].<ref>[http://physics.aps.org/authors/ernst_helmut_brandt Physics: Ernst Helmut Brandt]</ref>

He was born in [[Berlin-Kaulsdorf]], the second son of the [[publisher]] and [[bookseller]] Helmut Brandt and Elise Brandt (''née'' Stümpfle).<ref name="Huebener">Huebener, Rudolf P.; Morawetz, Klaus; Clem, John R. (2011) "[https://physicstoday.scitation.org/do/10.1063/PT.4.1660/full/ Obituary of Ernst Brandt (1941-2011)]", ''Physics Today'', 3 October 2011. Retrieved 29 January 2022</ref> He studied [[physics]] at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and [[Technische Universität Berlin]] and the [[Free University of Berlin]] between October 1961 to June 1967.<ref name="Huebener" /> He worked on his doctoral thesis under Professor [[:de:Alfred Seeger|Alfred Seeger]] at the [[Max Planck Institute]] for Metals Research and the University of Stuttgart between 1967 and 1969.<ref name="Huebener" /> From December 1969 to October 1970, he was a visiting scientist at the [[Lomonosov University]] in [[Moscow]]. In 1970, he was given a permanent position as researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Metals Research, Institute of Physics in Stuttgart, where he stayed until his retirement.<ref name="Huebener" /> He continued to travel and write publications after his retirement.<ref name="Huebener" />

He specialised in the theory of vortices in type-II superconductors.<ref name="Huebener" /> During his career he had over 330 publicationswith over 11,000 citations.<ref name="Huebener" />

He died on 1 September 2011 at his home, from inoperable [[pancreatic cancer]].<ref name="Huebener" />

==Personal life==
In 1970 he married Renate Sprandl.<ref name="Huebener" /> They had three children, Gerhard (born 1976), Ursula (born 1979), and Martin (born 1983).<ref name="Huebener" />
